method: The source is scaled to cover the output frame, so fit = max(frame width / source width, frame height / source height) and zoom z is a percentage of that fit: image scale = fit x z / 100, crop width = frame width / scale, crop height = frame height / scale. Zoom and both pan positions interpolate linearly over the frame index, and a pan value p places the crop centre at crop width / 2 + (p / 100) x (source width - crop width), so 0 is flush left and 100 is flush right. Frames = round(duration x frame rate), so the real clip is frames / frame rate. Image travel sums the per-frame centre movement scaled into output pixels; average speed divides that by the real clip duration and peak speed is the largest per-frame step times the frame rate. Oversampling is the tightest crop width divided by the frame width, so a value under 1 means the source is enlarged. Assumes a covered frame, no easing, no stabilisation and no rotation; a move smaller than one pixel per frame, or a crop below the frame size, will look stepped or soft in the rendered clip.
